comparables.description: RFF's own IFRS fair-value carrying amount: AUD 1,587M investment property at fair value as of June 30, 2025
comparables.source: RFF FY25 Annual Report — investment property at fair value

methodology:
Rural Funds Group is structurally different from the US REITs in the comp set: as an Australian REIT, RFF carries investment property at FAIR VALUE under IFRS — meaning book and FMV are by definition equal at AUD 1,587M as of June 30, 2025. The "book" column reflects this fair-value carrying amount.

The Properties table aggregates by sector since RFF doesn't publish per-property fair values in the Annual Report (each of 39 properties has individual independent valuations conducted at least every 24 months, but the per-asset detail isn't disclosed publicly). The aggregation: 3 almond orchards (4,139 planted ha), 21 cattle properties (672,342 ha — overwhelmingly the largest by area), 7 vineyards (666 ha), 6 macadamia orchards (3 mature + 3 development = 379 ha), 2 cropping properties (7,905 ha).

Comp anchors, all dated within 24 months:
- Australian almond orchards: $30-35K AUD/acre per Colliers Rural / LAWD H1 2025
- Queensland pastoral: $300-400 AUD/acre per Elders / LAWD 2024-2025 — RFF's massive cattle station acreage drives total area but is the lowest per-acre value in the portfolio
- Australian vineyards: $25-35K AUD/acre per wine industry reports
- Macadamia orchards: $45-55K AUD/acre — highest per-acre value in the portfolio
- Cropping ground: $4-5K AUD/acre per Rabobank trends

Because RFF's book value is already a fair-value mark, the FMV-vs-book premium displayed will be small and reflects only my per-sector assumptions vs. RFF's own appraisers. Implied NAV/share at FMV will closely match RFF's published NTA (AUD 2.21/unit). The Live-price-vs-NAV comparison is the more useful signal for RFF since it represents pure market-vs-NAV discount.
